Task guide

Admin guideline · version 2

Running Aurelia, one task at a time

You don’t need to learn every screen. Find what you want to do, follow the steps, and mind the one thing to watch out for. Written for someone new to the team.

New here? Start with these three things

1. What the admin isThe team’s website for running Aurelia: people, the study, content, AI, money and privacy. It’s part of the same app people use, at /admin.
2. How to get inOpen aureliaprod.vercel.app/admin (production) or the staging site’s /admin. Enter the site password; ask the product owner, it is never written down.
3. Nothing is real yetEvery number is realistic sample data, and your edits only last for this visit. Explore freely, but never quote a figure as a result.
Good to know: there is no admin login yet, so anyone with the address and password can open it (the top known gap). Staging is the test copy where new things land first; production is what the client sees. Both have sample data.

Your first 15 minutes

  1. Open the Dashboard and click one card: every figure takes you to the page that owns it.
  2. Open Users, search for any name, and open that person.
  3. Open Moderation and sort by severity.
  4. Open Feedback group · version 2 and look at the Milestones tab.
  5. Skim the sidebar once. It’s grouped by job: Overview, People, Experimentation, Content, Intelligence, Revenue, Growth, Platform.

Who can do what

Five team roles. Give each person the smallest one that does their job. Roles take effect once admin login exists.

RoleCanCan’t
Super AdminEverything, including roles and settingsBe reduced, so nobody can lock everyone out
OperationsDay-to-day work on people and content; read AI monitoringChange AI settings or roles, adjust coins
ModeratorReview and act on reportsEdit people, AI or money
AI EngineerModels, prompts, spend limitsEdit people or content
AnalystRead almost everything for reportingChange anything

Full permission matrix: version 1 of this guide, “Roles and permissions”, or Roles & permissions.

Every morning (10 minutes)

1 · Dashboard“Needs attention”: what is waiting on someone. Open
2 · ModerationAnything critical, and any self-harm or crisis report, first. Open
3 · ComplianceAny privacy request close to its deadline. Open
4 · AI monitoringErrors or spend going up. Open
5 · StudyIf the study is running: This week. Open

I want to…

Find your task, follow the steps. If it isn’t here, version 1 of this guide describes every screen in full.

People

Find someone

Where: Users

Steps
  1. Type a name or email in the search box.
  2. Use the filters (status, plan, role, country) to narrow it down.
  3. Click the row to open their page.
Watch out

Always find people by search or id, never by guessing from a name.

See one person’s history

Where: Users → a person

Steps
  1. Open the person from Users.
  2. Read their sessions, coins and the actions taken on their account.
Watch out

Their well-being panel is sample data today.

Change someone’s role, or suspend them

Where: Users

Steps
  1. Find the person.
  2. Pick a new role from the dropdown in their row, or press Suspend / Reactivate.
Watch out

It takes effect immediately. Only do it if your role allows it, and say why in your notes.

Invite a new team member

Where: Users → Invite user

Steps
  1. Press Invite user.
  2. Enter name, email and role, then Send invite.
Watch out

Give the smallest role that does the job (see “Who can do what”).

Check whether people feel better

Where: Well-being outcomes

Steps
  1. Read the cards: who improved, the average change, who needs a follow-up.
  2. Filter “follow-up” to see who scored 28 or less.
Watch out

A follow-up is for a person to make, never the app. A change here is not proof Aurelia caused it.

The feedback group study

Run the study day to day

Where: Feedback group · version 2 → This week

Steps
  1. Open This week every morning.
  2. Do the calls and follow-ups it lists, safety first.
  3. Use the Milestones tab to see whether the next checkpoint is on track.
Watch out

The full routine is in the Feedback group playbook (version 2 is the easiest read).

Write down a contact with a participant

Where: A participant’s page → Coaching log

Steps
  1. Open the participant (P01–P30).
  2. Add an entry: what they said, how they feel (1–5), the next step.
Watch out

Never write names or contact details. The log saves in your browser until the backend exists.

Content

Take a session off Explore

Where: Sessions

Steps
  1. Find the session.
  2. Press Unpublish in its row.
Watch out

It disappears from Explore and the community feed but stays in the author’s own library.

Create or change a challenge

Where: Challenges

Steps
  1. Press New challenge, or Edit on a row.
  2. Fill in title, summary, cover, days, minutes per day and points.
Watch out

Deleting asks you to confirm. The current design shows challenges without rankings.

Handle a report

Where: Moderation

Steps
  1. Sort by severity: critical first.
  2. Open the report and decide.
Watch out

Self-harm or crisis reports go to the on-call reviewer straight away, whatever their place in the queue.

AI

Check that the AI is healthy

Where: AI monitoring

Steps
  1. Look at the cards: error rate, slow requests (p95), refusals, quality score.
  2. Check daily spend by model.
Watch out

A rising error rate or spend is red. Tell the AI engineer.

Change what the chat replies

Where: Cockpit rules

Steps
  1. Find the rule whose trigger matches.
  2. Edit its reply or the prompts it offers.
Watch out

Order matters: the first matching rule wins. This becomes “AI policies” when real AI arrives.

Money

See how revenue is doing

Where: Revenue

Steps
  1. Read monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn and retention.
Watch out

All sample data; prices are not decided yet.

Find failed payments

Where: Payments → dunning queue

Steps
  1. Read the list of failed cards and their grace dates.
Watch out

No payment provider is connected yet.

Give or take coins

Where: Coins & rewards

Steps
  1. Find the entry in the ledger.
Watch out

Only with the coins.adjust permission. Every grant is written to the audit log.

Growth

Check an A/B test

Where: Experiments (A/B)

Steps
  1. Find the test; read its lift and confidence.
Watch out

This is product testing, not the feedback-group study. A test that has run long without confidence should be stopped.

Check a message campaign

Where: Notifications

Steps
  1. Read delivered, opened and converted for each campaign.
Watch out

Marketing messages need the person’s consent; payment or security messages do not.

Platform

Answer a privacy request (see or delete my data)

Where: Compliance & privacy

Steps
  1. Open the request; check its due date and owner.
Watch out

Overdue requests are a legal risk. They come before anything else on this page.

Change what a wearable reads

Where: Signal sources

Steps
  1. Edit the source’s name, group or what it reads.
Watch out

The “Reads” text is what people agreed to. Changing it means asking them again.

See who changed what

Where: Audit log

Steps
  1. Search by person, action or date.
Watch out

The log can’t be edited or deleted.

Change a platform setting

Where: Settings

Steps
  1. Pick the AI model, set the monthly spend ceiling, or switch a feature on or off.
Watch out

These are written to the audit log. The demo’s own switches live elsewhere.

Rules that always apply

Safety
  • Anything about health or harm goes to a person, the same day. Nothing is acted on automatically.
  • Self-harm and crisis reports skip the queue.
Care
  • Deleting or removing always asks you to confirm. Read it.
  • Important changes are written to the audit log.
  • Changing consent text means asking people again.
Honesty
  • Sample data is never quoted as a result.
  • Overdue privacy requests are a legal risk, not a to-do.
  • Find people by id or search, never by guessing.

Words you’ll see

Sample data
Realistic, generated numbers used until the backend exists.
Staging / production
The test copy of the site, and the real one the client sees.
WHO-5
A five-question well-being score from 0 to 100. +10 is a real change; 28 or less means a person follows up.
P01–P30
Code names for study participants. Real names never appear in the admin.
Coaching log
The project manager’s notes on each participant.
Cut / version
One built version of a session (v1.0, v1.1…).
MRR, churn
Monthly recurring revenue; the share of paying people who stop.
Dunning
Retrying a failed card payment before a subscription ends.
Privacy request (DSAR)
Someone asking to see, fix or delete their data. It has a legal deadline.
LLM-as-judge
An AI that scores a sample of the AI’s answers against a checklist.

What’s coming

  • First: real accounts, saved data, an admin login and the audit log.
  • Then: AI monitoring and AI policies on real model calls.
  • Later: payments, coins and challenges on real data, and every page on the database.
Start with the Dashboard, keep safety first, and ask before you change anything you can’t undo. Every screen in full detail is in version 1 of this guide.
